title: Detect high-confidence duplicates pre-claim and surface evidence (no close)
body:
## Background

A4.5 Check 4 (`idd-suitability.instructions.md`) detects duplicate or
superseded work with a deliberately weak title/declaration heuristic.
On a hit it is read-only: it may only report and optionally apply a
`triage:{outcome}` label, and its Mutation Policy explicitly forbids
closing the issue ("must NOT ... close issues unilaterally").

A stronger mechanical supersession signal already exists, but only in
B2.0 (`idd-work.instructions.md`) — a closing-PR reference, a merged PR
that changed the same files the issue scopes under `## Candidate files`,
or the issue's acceptance criteria already holding on current `main`.
B2.0 runs only **after** claim and B1 worktree creation.

The gap: when an issue frames a problem from a different angle than an
already-shipped sibling, A4.5's weak heuristic misses it, so the
duplicate proceeds to claim plus worktree before B2.0 can catch it —
paying claim and worktree cost — or, when B2.0 also misses the framing,
a redundant implementation begins. There is currently no **pre-claim**
path that applies B2.0's stronger signal, and no requirement that a
duplicate finding carry machine-derivable evidence.

This is Step 1 of a deliberately staged rollout: it only **detects and
evidences** pre-claim; it never closes. Authorizing an autonomous
pre-claim close is a separate, human-gated follow-up.

## Proposed change

Work on the A-phase suitability surface — edit the template source
`idd-template/.github/instructions/idd-suitability.instructions.md`
(A4.5 Check 4) and regenerate the `.github/instructions/` copy with
`node scripts/sync-docs.mjs --apply`; never hand-edit the generated
copy.

- Add a **high-confidence duplicate/superseded tier** to Check 4 that,
  in addition to the existing weak title/declaration heuristic,
  evaluates the same mechanical signals B2.0 documents:
  - the candidate issue is closed by or references a merged closing PR
    (`closedByPullRequestsReferences`), or
  - a PR merged at or after the candidate's relevant window changed a
    file the issue scopes under `## Candidate files` (reuse the existing
    `discover-shared-file-overlap` helper), and
  - where cheaply checkable, the issue's acceptance criteria already
    hold on current `main`.
- Prefer reusing or extracting B2.0's signal into a **shared, reusable
  check** so a later gated-close follow-up and B2.0 itself can gate on
  the identical signal. Do **not** change B2.0's existing post-claim
  runtime behavior in this issue; if a clean extraction is not
  low-risk, implement the pre-claim detection independently and leave
  the shared-check consolidation to the follow-up.
- When the high-confidence tier fires, surface the finding as **both**:
  - the existing `triage:duplicate` label, and
  - a diagnostic comment (prefixed "A4.5 suitability gate rejection",
    per the current Coordination Rule) that MUST include
    **machine-derivable evidence** — the merged or closing PR number
    and/or the overlapping file paths (with line anchors where
    applicable) — not a prose assertion alone.
- **Explicitly out of scope**: closing the issue, posting any claim or
  operational marker, and creating a branch or worktree. This issue
  must not cross A4.5's current no-close prohibition — it only
  strengthens detection and evidence.
- Keep behavior **fail-safe**: if the strong signal cannot be
  established mechanically, fall back to exactly today's behavior
  (weak-heuristic report, no new label or comment). Never fail toward a
  false high-confidence duplicate flag.

## Acceptance criteria

- A4.5 Check 4 in the template source, and its regenerated
  `.github/instructions/` copy, documents the high-confidence tier, the
  required machine-derivable evidence, and the explicit
  "detect-only, never close" boundary. `node scripts/sync-docs.mjs
  --apply` leaves no drift and `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check`
  passes.
- The strong-signal detection is exercised by helper-level tests
  (reusing or extending `discover-shared-file-overlap` and/or a new
  shared check), covering a closing-PR-reference hit, a
  same-candidate-files hit, and the no-signal fail-safe that reproduces
  today's behavior.
- No code path introduced here closes an issue, posts a claim or
  operational marker, or creates a branch or worktree; a test or an
  explicit review note confirms the detect-only boundary.
- `pre-push-validate` passes (biome, dprint, markdownlint, cspell,
  `idd-doctor`).

---

_Autopilot suitability: 4 / 5 -- higher is more autopilot-suitable;
below the configured floor is human-oriented._

_Effort: M -- author-estimated size; a soft autopilot selection
tie-breaker only._
